Description

Assigns the UniProt keyword KW-0418 (Kinase) through 1,392 alternative condition sets built from InterPro, PANTHER and CATH FunFam signatures.

The domain overlap table is not shown for this review. It is drawn from a cached analysis of the rule's condition sets, and the cache does not match the sets recorded here.

Review Summary

Accuracy: all 1,392 live condition sets were screened with two UniProtKB queries each (2026-11-10): the Swiss-Prot entries that match the whole conjunction, and how many of them carry KW-0418 (Kinase). Every set matches at least one Swiss-Prot entry, and all 46,549 set-level matches carry the keyword. The screen shows no conflict with curated keywords; it does not measure precision on the 3,762,398 unreviewed entries the rule annotates. Meaning and parsimony: Kinase is an enzyme class label and the first ten sets select kinase families (GHMP kinases, adenylate, thymidylate and cytidylate kinases, the amino acid kinase family, phosphoglycerate kinase, plant protein kinases), so the label fits and, for the many small-molecule kinases, it is the most specific keyword UniProt has. The keyword hierarchy has two narrower keywords, Serine/threonine-protein kinase and Tyrosine-protein kinase, each with its own ARBA rule; 648 of the 1,392 sets (47%) are structurally covered by a set of one of those two rules. Seen from above, 1,292 of the 1,392 sets are in turn covered by the Transferase rule ARBA00022679. Keywords stack and UniProt does not derive a parent keyword from a child, so those sets are what puts Kinase on protein kinases; the overlap is how the keyword system works, not a defect. All 1,392 sets are now recorded with their Swiss-Prot counts.

Action Rationale

Every one of the 1,392 condition sets has reviewed matches, and all 46,549 of them carry the keyword (rescanned 2026-11-15, counts recorded per set). The class label is coherent, and for small-molecule kinases it is the most specific keyword UniProt has. The overlap with the two protein-kinase keyword rules is not a parsimony defect, because the parent keyword is asserted by this rule and not inferred from the child. Confidence is not higher because the scan covers reviewed entries only; precision on the unreviewed entries the rule annotates is unmeasured.

Biological Meaning

COHERENT

Judged from the first 10 sets (those the accuracy pass read individually), which resolve into the five units below, together with the coverage count over all 1,392 sets and the screen of every set (46,549 of 46,549 Swiss-Prot matches carry the keyword). Each unit is a kinase family and the label is the narrowest keyword available for four of the five. For a class-label keyword the meaning question is answered by the label and the family sample, not by reading set 900; the scan of all 1,392 sets is what supports accuracy. Overlap with child-keyword rules is in keyword_redundancy.tsv; the GO fields do not apply (UniProt maps KW-0418 to GO:0016301 kinase activity).

The consequent term has descendant terms. 648 condition set(s) are also matched by a rule asserting a more specific term. 10 condition set(s) were examined for this judgement.

Assessments

ACCEPTABLE

Structural test on the 1,392 sets downloaded 2026-11-12: 648 sets are covered by a rule for a descendant keyword of KW-0418 (ARBA00022527 Serine/threonine-protein kinase 587; ARBA00023137 Tyrosine-protein kinase 69), and 1,292 are covered by a set of the parent rule ARBA00022679 (Transferase), 8 of the first 10 sets among them (all but sets 1 and 9). Keywords from the three rules stack on one protein (A0A1B0GXE3 carries all three, each with its own ARBA evidence). No set is subsumed by another set of the same rule. 1,004 sets are a single signature and 171 have a taxon condition. keyword_redundancy.tsv: 648 of 1,392 condition sets are also matched by a rule for a descendant keyword (Serine/threonine-protein kinase 587, Tyrosine-protein kinase 69; a set can be covered by more than one). Keywords from different rules stack on a protein, and UniProt does not derive a parent keyword from a child: in samples of 500 unreviewed entries each for Serine protease, Serine/threonine-protein kinase and Kinase (UniProtKB 2026_04, 2026-11-15) the parent keyword always carried its own rule evidence (ARBA, PROSITE-ProRule, HAMAP, PIRNR or RuleBase). So these sets do work: without them the proteins would lose this keyword.

APPROPRIATE

171 of 1,392 sets have a taxon condition; kinases occur in all domains of life. In the first ten sets the two taxon conditions are Bacteria on the GHMP N-terminal domain (set 1) and Viridiplantae on the protein kinase active-site signatures (set 5); both narrow a broad signature and neither was shown to exclude true kinases wrongly. Taxon conditions were not reviewed beyond the first ten sets.

Corrections (8)

Claims made by an earlier version of this review that were withdrawn, with the evidence that refuted them.

Withdrawn claimCorrection
The rule will annotate ATP-binding proteins, pseudokinases, helicases and chaperones as kinases.
unexamined rule · 2026-11-10		 No such protein was named and none was found among reviewed matches.
  • Previous version: condition_sets []
  • All 46,549 set-level Swiss-Prot matches of the 1,392 live sets carry KW-0418 (UniProtKB, 2026-11-10)
1,358 condition sets and 462 InterPro domains make the rule unsuitable; it should be removed.
size as evidence · 2026-11-10		 The number of condition sets is not evidence about correctness.
  • Live rule: 1,392 condition sets; every set has Swiss-Prot matches and all of them carry the keyword
The keyword Kinase gives no functional information and conflates distinct kinase classes.
general is not wrong · 2026-11-10		 It is a class label that is true of all of them; UniProt maps it to a GO molecular function term.
  • UniProt KW-0418 definition: Enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of phosphate (phosphoryl or pyrophosphoryl transfer) usually from ATP to a second substrate.
  • UniProt keyword KW-0418 geneOntologies: GO:0016301 kinase activity
Literature contradicts the rule because kinome studies classify kinases into families.
unsupported source · 2026-11-10		 A finer classification does not contradict the superclass label, and the only source cited was the rule's own manual note.
  • All previous supported_by entries cited rules/arba/ARBA00022777/ARBA00022777-deep-research-manual.md
The rule ignores taxonomy by covering bacteria, archaea, eukaryotes and viruses.
taxon misread · 2026-11-10		 Kinases occur in all of these, and part of the rule is taxon-restricted.
  • 171 of the 1,392 live condition sets have a taxon condition
The recommended action was REMOVE.
other · 2026-11-10		 REMOVE is not an action for a rule review, and the grounds given do not support retiring the rule.
  • RuleActionEnum: ACCEPT, MODIFY, DEPRECATE, SPLIT, MERGE, UNDECIDED
UNDECIDED, because a verdict on the whole rule needs every set to be read and precision on unreviewed entries to be measured.
meaning not judged · 2026-11-12		 The class label can be judged from the sample and the complete Swiss-Prot screen, and it fits. On parsimony, 648 of 1,392 sets are covered by rules for the two child keywords of Kinase. The verdict given then was MODIFY, to derive the keyword from its child keywords for those sets; that verdict is withdrawn in the next correction.
  • UniProt keyword KW-0418 Kinase: parent KW-0808 Transferase; children KW-0723 and KW-0829 (rest.uniprot.org/keywords, 2026-11-12)
  • ARBA rule set from rest.uniprot.org/arba/stream (2026-11-12): 648 of the 1,392 condition sets of ARBA00022777 are covered by a set of ARBA00022527 (587) or ARBA00023137 (69)
  • UniProtKB A0A1B0GXE3: KW-0418 evidence ARBA:ARBA00022777; KW-0723 evidence ARBA:ARBA00022527; KW-0808 evidence ARBA:ARBA00022679
The construction can be simplified: derive Kinase from its two child keywords and drop the 648 covered condition sets (MODIFY, 0.55).
other · 2026-11-15		 The count stands (648 of 1,392, keyword_redundancy.tsv) but it is not a defect. UniProt does not derive a parent keyword from a child, so dropping those sets would remove Kinase from the protein kinases they match.
  • UniProtKB 2026_04, 2026-11-15: of 500 unreviewed entries carrying KW-0723 (Serine/threonine-protein kinase), all carry KW-0418 (Kinase) with evidence of its own, an ARBA or other rule in nearly every case; none carries it with a derived tag.
  • A0A1B0GXE3 carries Transferase, Kinase and Serine/threonine-protein kinase, each with its own ARBA rule as evidence.

review_summary: >-
  Accuracy: all 1,392 live condition sets were screened with two UniProtKB queries each (2026-11-10):
  the Swiss-Prot entries that match the whole conjunction, and how many of them carry KW-0418 (Kinase).
  Every set matches at least one Swiss-Prot entry, and all 46,549 set-level matches carry the keyword.
  The screen shows no conflict with curated keywords; it does not measure precision on the 3,762,398 unreviewed
  entries the rule annotates. Meaning and parsimony: Kinase is an enzyme class label and the first ten
  sets select kinase families (GHMP kinases, adenylate, thymidylate and cytidylate kinases, the amino
  acid kinase family, phosphoglycerate kinase, plant protein kinases), so the label fits and, for the
  many small-molecule kinases, it is the most specific keyword UniProt has. The keyword hierarchy has
  two narrower keywords, Serine/threonine-protein kinase and Tyrosine-protein kinase, each with its own
  ARBA rule; 648 of the 1,392 sets (47%) are structurally covered by a set of one of those two rules.
  Seen from above, 1,292 of the 1,392 sets are in turn covered by the Transferase rule ARBA00022679. Keywords
  stack and UniProt does not derive a parent keyword from a child, so those sets are what puts Kinase
  on protein kinases; the overlap is how the keyword system works, not a defect. All 1,392 sets are now
  recorded with their Swiss-Prot counts.
action: ACCEPT
action_rationale: >-
  Every one of the 1,392 condition sets has reviewed matches, and all 46,549 of them carry the keyword
  (rescanned 2026-11-15, counts recorded per set). The class label is coherent, and for small-molecule
  kinases it is the most specific keyword UniProt has. The overlap with the two protein-kinase keyword
  rules is not a parsimony defect, because the parent keyword is asserted by this rule and not inferred
  from the child. Confidence is not higher because the scan covers reviewed entries only; precision on
  the unreviewed entries the rule annotates is unmeasured.
confidence: 0.7
suggested_modifications: []
biological_meaning:
  assessment: COHERENT
  notes: >-
    Judged from the first 10 sets (those the accuracy pass read individually), which resolve into the
    five units below,
    together with the coverage count over all 1,392 sets and the screen of every set (46,549 of 46,549
    Swiss-Prot matches carry the keyword). Each unit is a kinase family and the label is the narrowest
    keyword available for four of the five. For a class-label keyword the meaning question is answered
    by the label and the family sample, not by reading set 900; the scan of all 1,392 sets is what supports
    accuracy. Overlap with child-keyword rules is in keyword_redundancy.tsv; the GO fields do not apply
    (UniProt maps KW-0418 to GO:0016301 kinase activity).
  sets_examined_for_meaning: 10
  sets_covered_by_more_specific_rule: 648

parsimony:
  assessment: ACCEPTABLE
  notes: >-
    Structural test on the 1,392 sets downloaded 2026-11-12: 648 sets are covered by a rule for a descendant
    keyword of KW-0418 (ARBA00022527 Serine/threonine-protein kinase 587; ARBA00023137 Tyrosine-protein
    kinase 69), and 1,292 are covered by a set of the parent rule ARBA00022679 (Transferase), 8 of the
    first 10 sets among them (all but sets 1 and 9). Keywords from the three rules stack on one protein
    (A0A1B0GXE3 carries all three, each with its own ARBA evidence). No set is subsumed by another set
    of the same rule. 1,004 sets are a single signature and 171 have a taxon condition. keyword_redundancy.tsv:
    648 of 1,392 condition sets are also matched by a rule for a descendant keyword (Serine/threonine-protein
    kinase 587, Tyrosine-protein kinase 69; a set can be covered by more than one). Keywords from different
    rules stack on a protein, and UniProt does not derive a parent keyword from a child: in samples of
    500 unreviewed entries each for Serine protease, Serine/threonine-protein kinase and Kinase (UniProtKB
    2026_04, 2026-11-15) the parent keyword always carried its own rule evidence (ARBA, PROSITE-ProRule,
    HAMAP, PIRNR or RuleBase). So these sets do work: without them the proteins would lose this keyword.
taxonomic_scope:
